intro.title: Application for Full Stack Engineer – Expensify
intro.description: I'm applying for the Full Stack Engineer role you posted on LinkedIn. Explore this interactive timeline below to see my journey from graphic designer to full-stack engineer.

timeline.title: The Through-Line
timeline.content: I've spent my career chasing one simple idea: let computers handle the tedium so people can focus on creativity, ideas, and progress. That's why Expensify immediately resonated with me — your mission aligns perfectly with what I've been building toward my entire professional life.

timeline.title: From Artist to Engineer
timeline.content:
I didn't start as an engineer. I studied graphic design at East Carolina University and spent my early career in print. But I quickly realized that static design wasn't enough — I wanted to build things that moved and did something.

At a catalog company, I taught myself AppleScript and automated a three-month production process down to two weeks. I literally coded myself out of a job — but it set my career in motion.

timeline.title: QuarkXPress in the Browser
timeline.content:
Before React, before modern web frameworks, I was experimenting with building QuarkXPress-like document layouts directly in the browser. This was the era of IE6 and table-based layouts — the idea of rich document editing in a browser was considered impossible.

The PoC never shipped, but it taught me to question conventional wisdom about what browsers could do. Ten years later, tools like Google Docs proved the concept at scale.

timeline.title: Catalyst Workflow Solutions
bullets: Built a system to automate 100+ custom jewelry catalogs, reducing a 3-month process to 2 weeks
Developed a 600-page medical supply catalog automation tool used by a 12-person design team, integrating product data and images for end-to-end print production in under 2 weeks
Built custom CMS with over 75,000 downloads before discontinuing — a great product I simply didn't know how to market at the time
timeline.lesson: Lesson learned: Never walk away from a good idea too soon.

timeline.title: Lead Web Developer
bullets: Built and maintained public-facing web applications for sales and customer acquisition
Doubled online conversion rate by developing a predictive service-eligibility app using geolocation and customer data
Automated migration of 100,000 email accounts from in-house system to Google for Business (Gmail)

timeline.title: The KNN Story
timeline.content:
My proudest technical moment at Cavalier came when a third-party API for checking service availability proved too slow — killing our conversion funnel before customers could even sign up.

I implemented a K-Nearest Neighbor algorithm to predict service availability using geolocation and historical customer data. The result? Online conversions doubled overnight.

That experience taught me what I love most — solving real-world problems through smart automation and creative engineering. Sometimes the best solution isn't waiting for the API to respond — it's building your own intelligence layer.

timeline.title: Technical Lead / Solutions Architect
bullets: Technical lead on 90+ DoD and US Navy websites, including large-scale content migrations
Led rebuilds for major nonprofit and financial services clients
Architected enterprise CMS solutions (AEM, WordPress, Oracle WCC, Drupal) for federal and Fortune 500 clients

timeline.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Scaled ingestion pipelines to handle 10K+ products/day, growing inventory from 500K to 6M
Helped drive $1M+ annual revenue growth with a team of 5
Represented team at design/tech industry events

timeline.title: Life in Copenhagen
timeline.content:
Moving to Denmark for Iconfinder was my first experience living and working in Europe. I learned to navigate a new culture, work with a fully distributed international team, and appreciate the Danish concept of hygge — finding comfort and contentment in simple things.

It planted a seed: maybe my wife and I didn't have to stay in one place. Maybe we could build our lives anywhere. That seed is now growing into our move to France.

timeline.title: From Developer to Architect
timeline.content:
My CMS and web work opened the door to enterprise consulting at ICF, where I led major rebuilds for federal and Fortune 500 clients. Working with Adobe Experience Manager, WordPress, Oracle WebCenter, and Drupal taught me how to think at scale — migrating content, architecting solutions, and leading technical teams across 90+ websites.

Joining Iconfinder in Denmark was a shift from enterprise to startup — but it was exactly what I needed. I helped scale their platform from half a million to over six million assets, processing thousands of products daily, and contributing to over $1M in annual revenue growth. It reminded me why I fell in love with building software: the ability to create something that grows and impacts real people.

timeline.title: Independent Consultant
bullets: Managed a team of 4 devs to build and launch VectorIcons.net, a multi-vendor e-commerce marketplace
Built a serverless, event-driven pipeline integrating AWS and Dropbox for a high-volume UK creative agency, aggregating, converting, and organizing 200–300 POS proofs per day
Built e-commerce platforms, CMS integrations, and creative tooling (Figma/Adobe plugins) using Node.js and React

timeline.title: VectorIcons.net
timeline.content:
During my consulting years, I built VectorIcons.net — a multi-vendor marketplace for vector icons and illustrations. It's built on Next.js and Express, deployed on AWS with a serverless image-processing pipeline I designed myself.

More than just a business, it's a living lab where I test new technologies, architectures, and ideas — all centered around making creative work faster and more enjoyable. It's also a reminder of that lesson from my CMS days: don't walk away from a good idea too soon.

timeline.title: Next Chapter: France
timeline.content:
I've been studying French since I was 15 — first in high school, then independently for decades. My wife and I have been planning our move to France for years, and it's finally happening in 2025.

This move represents everything I've learned: build systems that let you work from anywhere, never stop learning, and pursue dreams even when they take decades to realize.

Je parle français — pas couramment, mais j'y travaille chaque jour !

timeline.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Engineered AWS IAM auditing solutions to maintain least-privileged security posture, using event-driven Go applications with SQS, Lambda, and Step Functions to monitor over 1M IAM roles nightly
Managed data pipelines streaming millions of rows daily
Built custom Go tooling to improve developer experience
Led code reviews, Agile ceremonies, and participated in quarterly on-call rotations
Managed multiple application stacks in CloudFormation Templates

timeline.title: The Invisible Work
timeline.content:
My work at Capital One is technically challenging and important. Ensuring security compliance across over a million IAM roles is critical infrastructure work that keeps systems safe and running smoothly.

But most of what we build is invisible. No one sees it, no one touches it directly. I miss creating things that people see and feel — tools that make their daily work easier, more intuitive, more human. That's why I keep building VectorIcons.net. That's why Expensify resonates with me.

timeline.title: Why Expensify
timeline.content:
Expensify's mission — helping people spend less time on tedious work and more on what matters — speaks to the very core of what drives me. You're solving the same problem I've been obsessed with my whole career: freeing people to focus on creativity, impact, and meaning.

From automating catalog production to building IAM auditing systems, I've always been drawn to eliminating friction and letting people do what they do best. That's what Expensify does at scale — and I want to be part of that mission.

On a personal level, my wife and I are moving to France next year — a dream we've been building toward for years. I've studied French since I was 15 (currently around B1/B2 level), and I'm excited by the idea of joining a globally distributed team that values autonomy, curiosity, and impact over geography.

timeline.title: Let's Build Something Great
timeline.content:
I'd love the chance to bring my experience and builder's mindset to Expensify — helping to craft tools that make people's work easier, more intuitive, and more human.

I'm available to start immediately.

Thank you for considering my application.

– Scott Lewis
